name: cancerproteome

identification.resolved_title: CancerProteome: a resource to functionally decipher the proteome landscape in cancer
identification.reasoning: Exact name match found via web search: a database literally named 'CancerProteome' published in the NAR Database Issue, hosted at Harbin Medical University (bio-bigdata.hrbmu.edu.cn/CancerProteome). No other database uses this exact name; distinguished from CPTAC (a consortium/data-generating program, not this curated re-analysis resource) and from CanProVar (a different, older proteogenomic variation database).

relevance.justification: Covers core BioThings entity types (protein/gene, drug, cancer/disease) with quantitative relations: differential protein & PTM expression in tumor vs. control per cancer type, and protein-drug sensitivity correlations (413 drugs from DepMap/GDSC). Structured, tabular, gene-symbol + UniProt-identified. Not full 5 because disease field uses free-text TCGA-style cancer abbreviations rather than MONDO/DOID identifiers.

novelty.justification: No existing BioThings API (mygene.info, mychem.info, myvariant.info, mydisease.info) or pending.api resource ingests quantitative proteome or PTM-level differential expression data, or protein-level drug-sensitivity correlations. This is protein-abundance/PTM data (distinct from gene expression, variant, or gene-annotation data already covered) plus 4,111 novel microproteins from ribo-seq ORFs not represented anywhere in BioThings.

openness.justification: CC BY-NC license (per paper); all six download files (cancer_names.txt, protein_inf.txt, microprotein_inf.txt, PTM_protein_inf.txt, PTM_microprotein_inf.txt, protein_durg_inf.txt) fetched successfully via HTTPS with no login/registration/API key. Site returns 403 to default curl user-agent (basic bot filtering) but 200 with a standard browser User-Agent header — not an access gate. Per evaluation-checklist.md, CC-BY-NC is PASS (3/5) for BioThings' academic/non-profit use context.

evidence.scope: Manually curated, re-analyzed mass-spectrometry proteomic and PTM data across 21 cancer types (7406 samples, 102 datasets from CPTAC/PDC, PRIDE, MassIVE.quant, PeptideAtlas, jPOST, Panorama, iProX): 31,120 proteins, 4,111 microproteins, 84,257 PTM sites, plus 413 drug-protein sensitivity correlations (DepMap/GDSC) and clinical survival analysis modules.
evidence.overlap: No direct overlap with existing BioThings sources; UniProt/gene-symbol identifiers used for cross-referencing overlap with mygene.info/UniProt gene-protein mapping (context only, not the novel content). COSMIC/OncoKB gene lists are referenced within the resource but are already in myvariant.info (COSMIC) — those are supporting annotations, not the core novel data.
identifiers_found: UniProt accession (embedded in protein field, e.g. P07686)
TCGA-style cancer abbreviation (cancer field, mapped via cancer_names.txt)
PDC study accession (source field, e.g. PDC000400)

license.name: CC BY-NC
restrictions: non-commercial re-use only, per paper text

api_info.record_coverage: no public REST/GraphQL API documented; web interface (Browse/Search) plus static Download page only

target_api: pending.api (new API recommended: biothings.transltr.io/cancerproteome or similar)
risks: License is CC BY-NC — non-commercial restriction should be confirmed acceptable per BioThings' academic/non-profit use, but flagged for downstream commercial API consumers per evaluation-checklist.md guidance
Disease field uses free-text TCGA-style abbreviations, not MONDO/DOID — will need a mapping table (cancer_names.txt provides Abbreviated.name -> Uniform.name, still requires manual MONDO crosswalk)
Site blocks default non-browser HTTP clients (403) unless a standard User-Agent header is sent — plugin dumper must set a browser-like User-Agent
No explicit terms-of-use or license text is displayed on the live site itself; license text is stated only in the published paper (potential paper-vs-site mismatch)
No API or versioned bulk archive; only a single static download snapshot per file with no visible update/versioning history observed on site
